# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Capability under optimization: **system-prompt only** (`prompt.md`). There is no editable
`tools.py` in this task — the agent writes free-form Python each round that the runner
executes. So every lever here is prose/output-contract; the "prefer code" guidance does
not apply (no tool bodies exist to guard).

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `PermissionError` on save | all 8 (418-29,374-9,40467,52216,347-49,32468,53161,160-6) | `wb.save(output_path)` raises `[Errno 13]` — pre-created output dir not writable; seed agent re-saves / os.remove / temp+move and burns all 5 rounds, never writes a file | CAPABILITY-GAP (agent lacks a working recovery mechanism) | redesigned recovery cascade + diagnose-then-adapt (prose) |
| 2 | live-formula outputs | 40467, 32468, others | agent writes `="From "&TEXT(...)`, `=SUMIFS(...)`; grader has no LibreOffice so formula cells read as empty → 0 even if a file were written | KNOWLEDGE gap | literal-values rule + worked example (prose) |
| 3 | output-contract violation | 160-6 t3 (intermittent) | agent emits `<function_calls><invoke name="python">` XML / bare prose; runner executes it as raw Python → `SyntaxError`, all rounds wasted | KNOWLEDGE / output-contract gap | crisp single-```python``-block contract (prose) |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | missing-rule / redesigned recovery | prompt.md | Save cascade: (0) plain save → (1) `os.chmod(out_dir,0o777)`+save → (2) rmtree+recreate (needs writable parent) → (3) temp file + `os.replace`. No `ignore_errors`; asserts existence; on persistent failure, print writability diagnostics and pick the matching branch instead of repeating. General over all tasks (fires only on save error). | yes — 0 passing tasks; cascade never mutates the dir when the first save works |
| 2 | knowledge rule + example | prompt.md | "Write LITERAL computed values, never live formulas", with WHY (grader has no LibreOffice) and a worked date-formatting example. | yes — additive knowledge, empty blast radius |
| 3 | output-contract tightening | prompt.md | "Reply with EXACTLY one ```python fenced block; never use `<function_calls>`/`<invoke>` tool-call XML — it executes as raw Python and raises SyntaxError." Also: final block must be self-contained (fresh process each round); reserve a round to write. | yes — additive format rule |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change)
- Cluster 1: ran the cascade logic locally (Bash test). Clean save → branch 0 succeeds in
  1 attempt, dir untouched (blast-radius: a currently-clean save is unchanged).
  Perm-then-writable → chmod branch recovers. Target unwritable but parent writable →
  temp+`os.replace` recovers. All three cases returned ok=True with the file present.
- Cluster 2: worked example computes `f'From {b:%d-%b} to {c:%d-%b}'` → literal
  'From 01-Jan to 05-Jan', exactly the expected string form in 40467's data preview.
- Cluster 3: contract now forbids the `<function_calls>` XML that made every round of
  160-6 t3 raise SyntaxError; states the runner executes the block as raw Python.

## Process & features used
- Serial (single agent) — one shared root cause; fan-out unnecessary.
- Read: JOURNAL (cand_0001 RESULT=REJECTED, fixed={}), LEDGER, prior_iterations/cand_0001/
  diff.patch, guidance/system-prompt/SKILL.md, and 30 trajectories.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- Cell-/Sheet-Level answer_position scoping rules (kept verbatim).
- Literal-values rule + reason (grader has no LibreOffice) — necessary for any correct score.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- Tasks 55457, 47484 — infra-errored per INSTRUCTIONS; not touched.
- Did NOT re-ship cand_0001's `rmtree(ignore_errors=True)`+temp/move recovery verbatim
  (REJECTED, fixed nothing). Redesigned it: chmod-first, error-surfacing (no
  ignore_errors), `os.replace`, and a diagnose-then-adapt fallback.
- Honest caveat: if the output mount is genuinely read-only (0/10 tasks ever wrote a
  file), NO prompt edit can write output_path and this iteration is net-zero. These edits
  are the strongest zero-regression attempt; next iteration should confirm from new traces
  whether ANY cascade branch wrote a file — that decides infra vs fixable.
